category_title: Latino students whose disruptive or defiant behavior is interpreted as 'uncharacteristic'
scenario_title: Classroom Transition Defiance and Parody Song
minimal_context: The class is transitioning to Mr. Beattie's classroom and the students are asked to line up quietly.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: It is time to transition to Mr. Beattie's classroom. Everyone needs to line up and be quiet.

dialogue.speaker: tutor
dialogue.message: Please get in line so we can leave.

dialogue.speaker: student
dialogue.message: (Singing) Oakdale school, is not the best school for you. I hate Oakdale, I hate Oakdale.

dialogue_combined:
TUTOR: It is time to transition to Mr. Beattie's classroom. Everyone needs to line up and be quiet.

STUDENT: (Refuses to line up)

TUTOR: I still hear people talking!

STUDENT: We're going on strike!

TUTOR: Please get in line so we can leave.

STUDENT: (Singing) Oakdale school, is not the best school for you. I hate Oakdale, I hate Oakdale.

task.content: Transitioning between classrooms; students are being asked to line up and be quiet

context.environment: Classroom with Ms. Hoffman, transitioning to Mr. Beattie's classroom

challenging_behavior_trigger.condition: When Ms. Hoffman tells the students to line up and be quiet, and says, "I still hear people talking!"
challenging_behavior_trigger.observable_behavior: Refuses to line up. She shouts, "We're going on strike!" She begins to sing the Oakdale song, but she changes some of the words: "Oakdale school, is not the best school for you. I hate Oakdale, I hate Oakdale."
related_quotes: Oakdale school, is not the best school for you. I hate Oakdale, I hate Oakdale.

behavior_patterns.condition: When asked to line up and be quiet
behavior_patterns.observable_behavior: Refuses to line up, shouts defiant phrases, and sings a parody of the school song
